edges.effect_quant: Aromatase inhibitors consistently lower bone mineral density in postmenopausal women. In the ATAC bone substudy, anastrozole produced median 5-year BMD declines of 6.08% at the lumbar spine and 7.24% at the total hip, whereas tamoxifen users had small BMD gains.
edges.population: postmenopausal women receiving adjuvant aromatase inhibitor therapy for hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer
edges.mechanism: Aromatase inhibitors markedly suppress peripheral estrogen production. Because estrogen is central to maintaining bone turnover balance in postmenopausal women, this pharmacologic estrogen deprivation accelerates bone resorption and drives loss of bone mineral density, especially at trabecular-rich sites such as the lumbar spine.
edges.summary: The evidence strongly supports a harmful effect on bone density. Across randomized substudies and prospective cohorts, aromatase inhibitors accelerate bone loss compared with tamoxifen, placebo, or healthy control trajectories, making bone monitoring and protective strategies important during therapy.
edges.caveats: The magnitude of loss varies by baseline bone status, menopausal recency, BMI, chemotherapy exposure, and concurrent bone-protective treatment. This edge reflects the untreated or minimally protected bone effect of aromatase inhibitor therapy, not what can be achieved when bisphosphonates or denosumab are used proactively.

evidence.citation: Eastell et al 2008 J Clin Oncol
evidence.notes: Effect of anastrozole on bone mineral density: 5-year results from the anastrozole, tamoxifen, alone or in combination trial 18233230.

effect_quant.comparator: median lumbar spine bone mineral density change from baseline to 5 years among anastrozole-treated women

evidence.notes: Estrogen-dependent increase in bone turnover and bone loss in postmenopausal women with breast cancer treated with anastrozole. Prevention with bisphosphonates.

effect_quant.comparator: mean lumbar spine bone mineral density change after 1 year of anastrozole in untreated surveillance patients

evidence.notes: Long-term effects of anastrozole on bone mineral density: 7-year results from the ATAC trial.

effect_quant.comparator: median lumbar spine bone mineral density change at year 7 after completing 5 years of anastrozole in evaluable ATAC follow-up participants

new_entities.name: Aromatase inhibitors
new_entities.description: Endocrine therapies that suppress estrogen production and are commonly used in postmenopausal hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.

new_entities.name: Bone mineral density
new_entities.description: A quantitative measure of bone mass, commonly assessed at the lumbar spine and hip to estimate skeletal strength and osteoporosis risk.
